written.label: Abdominal drain
written.definition: A drain that is placed in the abdominal cavity or in an abdominal surgical site to carry fluid, blood or air out of the abdomen.
written.why: Rests on the anatomical site of placement, which distinguishes it from other drains.

written.label: Activated carbon layer wound dressing
written.definition: A wound dressing that has as part a layer of activated carbon, a highly porous carbon that adsorbs volatile odour molecules released from the wound.
written.why: Rests on the activated carbon component, which distinguishes it from other wound dressings.

written.label: Active drain
written.definition: A drain that removes fluid or air from a wound or body cavity by negative pressure applied from a suction source, rather than by gravity or capillary action.
written.why: Rests on the established surgical distinction between suction (active) and passive drainage.

written.label: Adhesive silicone grid
written.definition: A silicone spacer grid whose silicone surface is tacky, so that it adheres to the skin around the wound without a separate fixation material.
written.why: Rests on the adhesive property of the silicone, which sets it apart from non-adhesive spacer grids.

written.label: Antiseptic alcohol
written.definition: A material used for wound treatment that is an alcohol, an organic compound bearing a hydroxyl group on a saturated carbon atom, and that bears the antiseptic drug role.
written.why: Rests on the chemical class alcohol plus the asserted antiseptic drug role axiom.

written.label: Alginate containing wound dressing
written.definition: A wound dressing that has as part fibres or a gel of alginate, a salt of alginic acid obtained from brown seaweed, which forms a gel on contact with wound exudate.
written.why: Rests on the alginate component and its gel-forming property, which distinguishes it from other wound dressings.

written.label: ANCA-associated Vasculitis
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting of necrotizing inflammation of the walls of predominantly small blood vessels, with few or no immune deposits, that is associated with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies.
written.why: Rests on the established nosological definition of ANCA-associated vasculitis (Chapel Hill consensus), framed as material inflamed vessel tissue.

written.label: Antibiotic therapy plan specification
written.definition: A treatment plan specification that prescribes the administration to a patient of one or more drugs bearing the antibiotic role, including the agent, route and duration.
written.why: Rests on the prescribed intervention being the administration of antibiotic drugs.

written.label: Antiseptic dye
written.definition: A material used for wound treatment that is a coloured compound that stains the tissue it is applied to and bears the antiseptic drug role.
written.why: Rests on the chemical class dye (coloured, staining compound) plus the asserted antiseptic drug role axiom.

written.label: Antiseptic halogen-releasing compound
written.definition: A material used for wound treatment that is a chemical compound releasing an oxidizing halogen species on application and bears the antiseptic drug role.
written.why: Rests on halogen release as the chemical feature plus the asserted antiseptic drug role axiom.

written.label: Antiseptic metal ion
written.definition: A material used for wound treatment that consists of positively charged metal atoms, or of a material releasing them, and bears the antiseptic drug role.
written.why: Rests on the chemical nature as metal cations plus the asserted antiseptic drug role axiom.

written.label: Antiseptic phenol derivative
written.definition: A material used for wound treatment that is a compound structurally derived from phenol, having a hydroxyl group bonded directly to an aromatic ring, and bears the antiseptic drug role.
written.why: Rests on the phenolic chemical structure plus the asserted antiseptic drug role axiom.

written.label: Antiseptic solution
written.definition: A wound irrigation solution that contains a dissolved substance bearing the antiseptic drug role.
written.why: Rests on the presence of an antiseptic solute, which distinguishes it from non-antiseptic irrigation fluids such as saline.

written.label: Arterial leg ulcer
written.definition: A skin wound located on the leg or foot in which the skin and underlying tissue are disrupted in an area that is ischaemic owing to insufficient arterial blood supply.
written.why: Rests on the lower-limb location and the arterial ischaemic nature that define arterial ulcers in wound care.

written.label: ASEPSIS score
written.definition: A wound classification scale that grades a surgical wound for infection by summing points for additional treatment, serous discharge, erythema, purulent exudate, separation of deep tissues, isolation of bacteria and prolonged inpatient stay.
written.why: Rests on the published components of the ASEPSIS acronym and its use for scoring surgical wound infection.

written.label: Aseptic conditions plan specification
written.definition: A wound treatment plan specification that prescribes that wound treatment be carried out with sterile instruments, materials and techniques so that microorganisms are not introduced into the wound.
written.why: Rests on the prescribed asepsis requirement, which distinguishes it from other wound treatment plans.

written.label: Assessing patient's medical history
written.definition: A diagnostic process to assess wound characteristics in which information on the patient's past and current diseases, treatments and the origin and course of the wound is obtained from the patient, relatives or records.
written.why: Rests on the obtaining of anamnestic information as part of wound assessment, distinct from physical inspection or measurement of the wound.

written.label: Autolytic wound debridement process
written.definition: A debridement process in which necrotic tissue and slough are broken down by the patient's own enzymes and phagocytic cells in a wound kept moist.
written.why: Rests on the endogenous mechanism of tissue removal, which distinguishes it from surgical, mechanical, enzymatic and biological debridement.

written.label: Biobag debridement plan specification
written.definition: A biosurgical debridement plan specification that prescribes applying the sterile fly larvae to the wound enclosed in a sealed mesh bag, so that the larvae do not move freely over the wound surface.
written.why: Rests on the established distinction between contained (bagged) and free-range larval therapy.

written.label: Wound specimen procurement by biopsy process
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process in which a sample of tissue is cut or punched from the wound bed or wound edge and that has as specified output a wound tissue specimen for laboratory examination.
written.why: Rests on the meaning of biopsy as tissue removal for examination, set against the sibling's measurement output.

written.label: Biosurgical debridement plan specification
written.definition: A treatment plan specification that prescribes removing necrotic or devitalized tissue from a wound by applying live sterile fly larvae to it.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of biosurgical (larval or maggot) debridement therapy.

written.label: Biosurgical wound debridement process
written.definition: A debridement process in which live sterile fly larvae applied to a wound remove its necrotic or devitalized tissue.
written.why: Rests on the larvae being the agent that removes tissue, which sets this process apart from surgical, enzymatic, autolytic and mechanical debridement.

written.label: Biosynthetic cellulose
written.definition: A wound dressing whose wound-contacting material is a cellulose membrane synthesized by bacteria.
written.why: Rests on biosynthetic cellulose being bacterially produced cellulose, which is used as a dressing membrane.

written.label: Bite wound
written.definition: A traumatic wound that is the output of a wound causing trauma process in which the teeth of a human or an animal penetrate, tear or crush the tissue.
written.why: Rests on the kind of causing trauma, a bite by teeth, within the parent's definition.

written.label: Blake drain
written.definition: A low-vacuum drain consisting of a silicone tube whose intracorporeal portion has open longitudinal channels around a solid core instead of side holes.
written.why: Rests on the fluted, channelled design that distinguishes this drain from perforated tube drains.

written.label: Blistering skin wound
written.definition: A skin wound in which the skin layers separate within the epidermis or at the dermo-epidermal junction, and fluid collects in the resulting cavity.
written.why: Rests on the cleavage of skin layers with fluid accumulation that characterizes blistering.

written.label: Bovine collagen containing wound dressing
written.definition: A wound-integrating wound dressing that has as part collagen derived from cattle.
written.why: Rests on the bovine source of the collagen component.

written.label: Bromelain
written.definition: A substance used for enzymatic wound debridement that consists of a mixture of cysteine proteases extracted from the pineapple plant (Ananas comosus).
written.why: Rests on the established composition and source of bromelain.

written.label: Bullosis diabeticorum
written.definition: A material disease entity that has as parts one or more spontaneously arising, non-inflammatory skin blisters in a patient who has a diabetic metabolic disorder.
written.why: Rests on the clinical definition of diabetic bullae as spontaneous non-inflammatory blisters in diabetes, in the style of the blister-based sibling.

written.label: Bullous impetigo
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting of a superficial Staphylococcus aureus infection of the epidermis that has as parts one or more flaccid subcorneal blisters.
written.why: Rests on the established definition of bullous impetigo as a staphylococcal epidermal infection with superficial bullae.

written.label: Bülau drain
written.definition: A thoracic drain whose external end is placed under water in a collecting container, forming an underwater seal that lets air and fluid leave the pleural cavity while preventing their return.
written.why: Rests on the underwater-seal principle that defines Bülau chest drainage.

written.label: Capillary drain
written.definition: A passive drain that conducts wound fluid out of the wound by capillary action along narrow spaces within or between its fibres or channels, rather than through a single open lumen.
written.why: Rests on capillary action as the drainage mechanism, as opposed to gravity or pressure-driven flow through a lumen.

written.label: Cat bite wound
written.definition: A bite wound inflicted by the teeth of a cat.
written.why: Rests on the species of the biting animal.

written.label: Cellulose acetate mesh impregnated with a petrolatum emulsion
written.definition: A wound dressing that is a non-adherent wound contact layer formed by a knitted mesh of cellulose acetate fibres coated with an emulsion of petrolatum.
written.why: Rests on the dressing's material composition and its role as a non-adherent contact layer.

written.label: Clinical inspection
written.definition: A diagnostic process to assess wound characteristics in which a clinician directly observes the wound and the periwound skin by eye.
written.why: Rests on inspection meaning direct visual examination, which sets it apart from palpation, measurement and laboratory or imaging methods.

written.label: Clinical wound assessment
written.definition: A diagnostic process to assess wound characteristics in which a healthcare professional evaluates the wound, the periwound skin and the patient by history taking and physical examination at the point of care.
written.why: Rests on clinical assessment being the comprehensive bedside evaluation that includes inspection among its parts, as opposed to laboratory or imaging investigation.

written.label: Closed drain
written.definition: A drain whose external end is connected to a sealed collecting container or system, so that the drained fluid is not exposed to the environment.
written.why: Rests on the sealed connection to a collection system, which distinguishes closed drains from open drains.

written.label: CO2 bath wound therapy plan specification
written.definition: A wound treatment plan specification that prescribes a bath in which the wound-bearing body part is exposed to carbon dioxide, either dissolved in water or as a gas.
written.why: Differentia rests on the defining feature of the therapy, exposure of the wound region to carbon dioxide in a bath, covering both the water and gas forms.

written.label: Cold plasma wound treatment process
written.definition: A wound treatment process in which a non-thermal, partially ionized gas generated at atmospheric pressure is applied to the wound.
written.why: Differentia rests on the established meaning of cold plasma as non-thermal atmospheric-pressure ionized gas applied to tissue.

written.label: Compress debridement plan specification
written.definition: A mechanical debridement plan specification that prescribes removing necrotic tissue, slough and debris from the wound bed by wiping or lifting them off with compresses.
written.why: Differentia rests on the compress being the instrument of the mechanical removal, which distinguishes it from other mechanical debridement methods.

written.label: Compression therapy plan specification
written.definition: A wound treatment plan specification that prescribes applying sustained external pressure to the wound-bearing limb or body part by means of bandages, garments or devices.
written.why: Differentia rests on the defining element of compression therapy, sustained external pressure applied to the affected body part.

written.label: Continuous suture
written.definition: A suture in situ in which a single uninterrupted strand of suture material passes repeatedly through the tissue along the wound and is knotted only at its two ends.
written.why: Differentia rests on the single unbroken strand knotted only at its ends, which distinguishes it from interrupted sutures.

written.label: CUSA(r) assisted debridement
written.definition: An ultrasound-assisted wound debridement process that uses an ultrasonic surgical aspirator, which fragments tissue by ultrasonic vibration while simultaneously irrigating the site and aspirating the fragments.
written.why: Differentia rests on the generic device type designated by the trademark, combining ultrasonic fragmentation with irrigation and aspiration; the brand name is left out.

written.label: Debridement process
written.definition: A wound cleansing process in which necrotic or devitalized tissue, slough, foreign material and debris are removed from the wound.
written.why: Differentia rests on removing devitalized tissue as well as loose material, which sets debridement apart from other forms of wound cleansing.

written.label: Diagnostic process to assess wound characteristics
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process in which the wound itself is examined and that has as specified output data about qualities of that wound.
written.why: Differentia rests on the wound itself being both the object examined and the subject of the output, as opposed to processes assessing surrounding structures such as blood supply.

written.label: Dog bite wound
written.definition: A bite wound that was inflicted by the teeth of a dog.
written.why: Differentia rests on the causing animal, which distinguishes it from the other bite wounds.

written.label: Doppler sonographic diagnostic process
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process that uses ultrasound and the frequency shift of waves reflected from moving blood to assess blood flow in the vessels supplying the wound region.
written.why: Differentia rests on the established method of Doppler sonography, measuring blood flow through the ultrasound frequency shift.

written.label: Drain
written.definition: A material used for wound treatment that is a device placed in a wound or surgical site to conduct accumulated fluid or air out of it.
written.why: Differentia rests on the drain's defining function of conducting fluid or air out of a wound.

written.label: Dressing change plan specification
written.definition: A wound treatment plan specification that prescribes removing the wound dressing currently applied to a wound and applying a new one.
written.why: Differentia rests on the planned replacement of an existing dressing with a new one.

written.label: Dry necrosis
written.definition: A necrotic material that has lost its water content and is firm to hard in consistency.
written.why: Differentia rests on dehydration and hardness, which distinguish dry necrosis from moist or liquefied necrotic material.

written.label: Easy-Flow drain
written.definition: A capillary drain consisting of a flat, flexible tube with longitudinal internal grooves along which wound fluid flows passively out of the wound.
written.why: Differentia rests on the established design of this drain type, a flat, internally grooved flexible tube.

written.label: Elastic bandage
written.definition: A fixing bandage made of a material that can be stretched lengthwise and returns to its original length when released.
written.why: Differentia rests on the extensibility and recovery of the bandage material.

written.label: Enzymatic wound debridement process
written.definition: A debridement process in which necrotic tissue and slough are broken down and removed by topically applied proteolytic enzymes.
written.why: Differentia rests on enzymes being the debriding agent, as opposed to mechanical, surgical or other means.

written.label: Epithelialization process
written.definition: A wound healing related physiological process in which epithelial cells migrate, proliferate and differentiate across the wound surface until it is covered by a new epithelium.
written.why: Differentia rests on the established meaning of re-epithelialization as the restoration of an epithelial covering over the wound.

written.label: Exudation process
written.definition: A wound healing related physiological process in which fluid containing plasma proteins and cells passes from blood vessels into the wound tissue and onto the wound surface.
written.why: Differentia rests on the outflow of fluid from vessels that forms wound exudate.

written.label: Fat gauze
written.definition: A wound dressing consisting of a wide-meshed gauze impregnated with a fatty or ointment-based substance that reduces its adherence to the wound surface.
written.why: Differentia rests on the fat impregnation of the gauze and its design purpose of limiting adhesion.

written.label: Fibrin coating of the wound
written.definition: A material entity consisting of a layer of fibrin, formed from fibrinogen in wound exudate, that adheres to the surface of a wound bed.
written.why: Differentia rests on fibrin being the composing material and on its location as a coating of the wound bed; the general parent fits.

written.label: fistula
written.definition: A material disease entity that is an abnormal tract connecting two hollow organs, body cavities or vessels, or connecting one of these with the body surface.
written.why: Rests on the established medical meaning of fistula as an abnormal communicating passage between epithelialized or endothelialized surfaces.

written.label: Fixed drug exanthema
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting of one or more sharply demarcated inflammatory lesions of the skin or mucosa that arise as a hypersensitivity reaction to a drug and recur at the same sites each time the patient is re-exposed to that drug.
written.why: Rests on the defining features of fixed drug eruption: drug-induced hypersensitivity lesions that recur at fixed sites on re-exposure.

written.label: Fixing bandage
written.definition: A wound dressing that is a strip or tube of flexible material applied around a body part to hold another wound dressing in place over a wound.
written.why: Rests on the wound-care meaning of a fixing (retention) bandage, whose distinguishing role is securing a primary dressing.

written.label: Flaminal
written.definition: A wound gel/ointment/cream that is an alginate hydrogel containing the enzymes glucose oxidase and lactoperoxidase.
written.why: Rests on the published composition of this enzyme alginogel product, stated without brand names or claims of effect.

written.label: Flap plasty plan specification
written.definition: A wound treatment plan specification that prescribes closing or covering a wound by moving tissue from a donor site to the wound together with its own blood supply.
written.why: Rests on the surgical meaning of flap plasty: transfer of vascularized tissue, which distinguishes it from grafting.

written.label: Fournier's gangrene
written.definition: A material disease entity that is a necrotizing infection of the fascia and soft tissues of the perineal, genital or perianal region.
written.why: Rests on the established definition of Fournier's gangrene as necrotizing fasciitis confined to the perineal, genital and perianal region.

written.label: Friction bubble
written.definition: A material disease entity that is a fluid-filled cleft within the epidermis formed by repeated frictional shear forces acting on the skin.
written.why: Rests on the dermatological meaning of a friction blister: an intraepidermal blister produced by frictional shear.

written.label: Full-thickness skin graft
written.definition: A skin graft that consists of the entire epidermis and the entire dermis of the donor site.
written.why: Rests on the surgical distinction from split-thickness grafts: the graft includes the full depth of the dermis.

written.label: Gauze bandage
written.definition: A fixing bandage that is a roll of thin, loosely woven or knitted fabric with an open mesh.
written.why: Rests on the material of the bandage, an open-weave textile, which distinguishes it from other fixing bandages.

written.label: Germ spectrum assessment process
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process that has as specified output a datum identifying the microorganisms present in a sample of wound material.
written.why: Rests on the meaning of germ spectrum assessment as microbiological identification of the organisms colonizing or infecting a wound.

written.label: Granulation tissue formation process
written.definition: A wound healing related physiological process in which new connective tissue rich in capillaries and fibroblasts grows from the wound base and fills the wound bed during the proliferative phase of healing.
written.why: Rests on the histological and physiological meaning of granulation; the sibling scarring process covers the later fibrous replacement.

written.label: Gravity drain
written.definition: A passive drain that conducts fluid out of a wound by gravitational flow into a collecting receptacle positioned below the level of the wound.
written.why: Rests on gravity being the sole driving force, which distinguishes it from passive drains relying on capillary action or pressure differences.

written.label: Gustilo and Anderson wound classification
written.definition: A wound classification scale that stratifies the wounds of open fractures by wound size, extent of soft-tissue damage, degree of contamination and presence of arterial injury requiring repair.
written.why: Rests on the published criteria of the Gustilo and Anderson classification of open fractures.

written.label: Gustilo and Anderson wound classification grade
written.definition: A wound classification grade that is a category of the Gustilo and Anderson wound classification.
written.why: Follows the sibling pattern of defining a grade as a category of its named scale.

written.label: Hematoma
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting of a localized accumulation of blood that has escaped from blood vessels into a tissue, an organ or a body space.
written.why: Rests on the established medical meaning of hematoma as a circumscribed collection of extravasated blood.

written.label: High-vacuum drain
written.definition: An active drain that draws fluid out of a wound by means of high negative pressure held in a sealed, evacuated collection container.
written.why: Rests on high negative pressure from a pre-evacuated container being what distinguishes this type from low-vacuum and other active drains.

written.label: Histopathological examination process of wound material
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process in which tissue taken from a wound is fixed, sectioned, stained and examined microscopically to determine its cellular and structural characteristics.
written.why: Rests on the standard meaning of histopathological examination applied to wound tissue as specified input.

written.label: Horizontal mattress suture
written.definition: A suture in situ in which each stitch crosses the wound twice, entering and leaving the skin on both sides of the wound, so that the exposed thread segments lie parallel to the wound edge and the knot lies on one side of the wound.
written.why: Rests on the surgical configuration of the horizontal mattress stitch, which distinguishes it from simple and vertical mattress sutures.

written.label: Human bite wound
written.definition: A bite wound inflicted by the teeth of a human.
written.why: Rests on the human origin of the bite, which distinguishes it from animal bite wounds.

written.label: Hydrocolloid containing wound dressing
written.definition: A wound dressing that has as part a hydrocolloid, a hydrophilic colloidal material held in an adhesive matrix that forms a gel on contact with wound exudate.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of hydrocolloid dressings: the gel-forming hydrocolloid component is what distinguishes them from other dressings.

written.label: Hydrofiber-containing wound dressing
written.definition: A wound dressing that has as part a hydrofiber, a nonwoven layer of gelling carboxymethylcellulose fibres that absorb wound exudate and turn into a cohesive gel.
written.why: Rests on the composition of hydrofiber material, gelling carboxymethylcellulose fibres, which sets these dressings apart from other dressing types.

written.label: Hydrogel containing wound dressing
written.definition: A wound dressing that has as part a hydrogel, a cross-linked network of hydrophilic polymers with a high water content.
written.why: Rests on the defining hydrogel component, a water-swollen hydrophilic polymer network.

written.label: Hyperbaric O2 wound therapy plan specification
written.definition: A wound treatment plan specification that prescribes that the patient breathe oxygen while inside a chamber pressurized above atmospheric pressure.
written.why: Rests on the standard meaning of hyperbaric oxygen therapy: oxygen breathed at greater than atmospheric pressure in a pressurized chamber.

written.label: Hypergranulation
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting of granulation tissue in a wound bed that has proliferated above the level of the surrounding skin surface.
written.why: Rests on the clinical meaning of hypergranulation: excess granulation tissue raised above the wound margin.

written.label: Excessive collagen deposition process
written.definition: A scarring process in which collagen is laid down in excess of the amount needed to replace the tissue lost in the wound, yielding a raised scar.
written.why: Rests on the label and the hypertrophic scarring synonym: excess collagen deposition producing a raised scar distinguishes it from ordinary scarring.

written.label: Incision foil
written.definition: A material entity that is an adhesive polymer film applied to the skin over a surgical site, through which the surgical incision is made.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of incision foil (incise drape) in surgery.

written.label: Intact wound margin
written.definition: A wound edge whose skin is continuous and shows no maceration, erosion, inflammation or other damage.
written.why: Rests on the wound-assessment meaning of an intact margin: undamaged skin at the edge, in contrast to the macerated, reddened and livid sibling edges.

written.label: Intracutaneous suture
written.definition: A suture in situ that runs within the dermis along the wound edges and, between its ends, does not pass through the epidermal surface.
written.why: Rests on the surgical meaning of intracutaneous (intradermal) suturing: the stitch placement lies within the dermis.

written.label: Iodine ointment
written.definition: A wound gel/ointment/cream that is an ointment with iodine or an iodine-releasing compound as its active ingredient.
written.why: Rests on the label: an ointment whose distinguishing active ingredient is iodine.

written.label: Jackson-Pratt drain
written.definition: A low-vacuum drain consisting of a perforated flexible tube connected to a compressible bulb reservoir whose re-expansion after manual compression produces the suction.
written.why: Rests on the established construction of the Jackson-Pratt drain: a perforated tube attached to a bulb reservoir.

written.label: Keloid development process
written.definition: A pathological scarring process in which collagen is deposited beyond the margins of the original wound into the surrounding skin, yielding a raised scar that extends past the wound boundaries.
written.why: Rests on the defining feature of keloid formation, scar growth beyond the original wound margins, which distinguishes it from hypertrophic scarring.

written.label: Linear IgA dermatosis
written.definition: A material disease entity that has as parts one or more subepidermal blisters that are immune-mediated tissue disorders marked by linear deposits of IgA antibodies along the epidermal basement membrane zone.
written.why: Rests on the established definition of linear IgA dermatosis and follows the style of the mucous membrane pemphigoid sibling.

written.label: Livedovasculopathy
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting of occlusive thrombi in small blood vessels of the dermis, without primary inflammation of the vessel walls.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of livedoid vasculopathy: a non-inflammatory, thrombo-occlusive disorder of dermal vessels.

written.label: Process of administering a local anesthetic agent
written.definition: A process of drug administration in which a material entity bearing a local anesthetic drug role participates.
written.why: Rests on the logical axiom and mirrors the antibiotic administration sibling.

written.label: Low-vacuum drain
written.definition: An active drain that draws fluid out of a wound or body cavity under a mild negative pressure, weaker than that applied by a high-vacuum drain.
written.why: Rests on how drains are classified in wound care: the low level of suction separates these drains from high-vacuum active drains.

written.label: Lymphatic fistula
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting of an abnormal passage that connects a lymphatic vessel or lymph node with the body surface or another anatomical structure and through which lymph leaks.
written.why: Rests on the medical meaning of fistula, applied to the lymphatic system.

written.label: Manuka honey
written.definition: A medicinal honey produced by bees from the nectar of the manuka tree, Leptospermum scoparium.
written.why: Rests on the botanical origin that defines manuka honey.

written.label: Marjolin ulcer
written.definition: A skin wound that is an ulcerated malignant neoplasm arising in scar tissue or in a long-standing chronic wound.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of Marjolin ulcer: malignant transformation within a scar or chronic wound.

written.label: Material used for wound treatment
written.definition: A material entity that is intended to be applied to or placed in a wound in the course of a wound treatment process.
written.why: Rests on the intended use of the material in wound care, which distinguishes it from role-defined siblings such as trace element.

written.label: Mechanical debridement plan specification
written.definition: A treatment plan specification that prescribes the removal of non-viable tissue, debris and foreign material from a wound by physical force applied to the wound bed, without cutting and without enzymatic, autolytic or biological agents.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of mechanical debridement as physical, non-sharp, non-enzymatic removal of non-viable material.

written.label: Mechanical wound debridement process
written.definition: A debridement process in which non-viable tissue, debris and foreign material are removed from a wound by physical force applied to the wound bed, without cutting and without enzymatic, autolytic or biological action.
written.why: Distinguishes mechanical debridement from sharp, surgical, enzymatic, autolytic and biological debridement by its physical, non-cutting mode of removal.

written.label: Medicinal honey
written.definition: A material used for wound treatment that consists of honey that has been filtered and sterilised to a standard for medical application to wounds.
written.why: Rests on medicinal honey being honey processed and sterilised for clinical use, unlike ordinary food honey.

written.label: Wound treatment plan specification
written.definition: A medical condition treatment plan specification that prescribes actions to be carried out on or for a wound with the aim of promoting its healing or preventing its deterioration.
written.why: Rests on the wound being the condition the plan's prescribed actions are directed at.

written.label: Microangiopathy
written.definition: An angiopathy in which the abnormal structure of the vessel wall or lumen affects small blood vessels, namely arterioles, capillaries or venules.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of microangiopathy as angiopathy confined to the small vessels, in contrast to macroangiopathy.

written.label: Microbial analysis of the wound swab for wound pathogens
written.definition: A diagnostic process to assess wound characteristics in which a specimen collected from the wound with a swab is examined in a laboratory to detect and identify microorganisms that cause wound infection.
written.why: Rests on the specimen type (wound swab) and the laboratory microbiological examination for pathogens.

written.label: Moist necrosis
written.definition: A necrotic material that has a high water content and a soft, wet consistency, in contrast to dry, hardened necrotic tissue such as eschar.
written.why: Rests on the wet, soft consistency that distinguishes moist necrosis from dry necrosis.

written.label: Monaldi drain
written.definition: A thoracic drain that is inserted through the anterior chest wall at the second intercostal space in the midclavicular line.
written.why: Rests on the Monaldi insertion site, which distinguishes it from thoracic drains placed in the lateral (Bülau) position.

written.label: Monofilament thread material
written.definition: A material entity that is suture thread consisting of a single strand, rather than of several filaments braided or twisted together.
written.why: Rests on the single-strand structure that distinguishes monofilament from multifilament suture thread.

written.label: n-propanol
written.definition: An antiseptic alcohol that consists of propan-1-ol, the unbranched primary alcohol with three carbon atoms.
written.why: Rests on the chemical identity of n-propanol, distinguishing it from other antiseptic alcohols such as ethanol and isopropanol.

written.label: NaCl 0.9%
written.definition: A wound irrigation solution that is an aqueous solution of sodium chloride at a concentration of 0.9% (w/v), isotonic with body fluids.
written.why: Rests on the solute and concentration named in the label, which make the solution isotonic.

written.label: NaCl 10%
written.definition: A wound irrigation solution that is an aqueous solution of sodium chloride at a concentration of 10% (w/v), hypertonic relative to body fluids.
written.why: Rests on the solute and concentration named in the label, which make the solution hypertonic.

written.label: Negative pressure wound therapy plan specification
written.definition: A wound treatment plan specification that prescribes the application of sub-atmospheric pressure to the wound bed through an airtight dressing connected to a suction source.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of negative pressure wound therapy as controlled sub-atmospheric pressure applied via a sealed dressing.

written.label: Non-absorbable thread material
written.definition: A material entity that is suture thread which is not broken down and absorbed by the body's tissues and so persists in the tissue unless it is removed.
written.why: Rests on the lack of biodegradation in tissue that distinguishes non-absorbable from absorbable suture thread.

written.label: Nutritional status improvement process
written.definition: A wound treatment process in which the dietary or supplementary nutrient intake of a patient who has a wound is changed with the aim of correcting a deficiency or imbalance of nutrients in the patient's body.
written.why: Rests on the process acting on the patient's nutrient intake rather than directly on the wound.

written.label: Octenidine gel
written.definition: A wound gel/ointment/cream that has a gel consistency and contains octenidine dihydrochloride as its antiseptic active substance.
written.why: Rests on the gel formulation and the octenidine active ingredient that distinguish it from other wound gels, ointments and creams.

written.label: Open drain
written.definition: A drain that discharges fluid from a wound or body cavity into an absorbent dressing or the surroundings rather than into a sealed collection container.
written.why: Rests on the absence of a closed collection system, which distinguishes open from closed drains.

written.label: Pain management plan specification
written.definition: A medical condition treatment plan specification that prescribes pharmacological or non-pharmacological measures to prevent or reduce pain experienced by the patient.
written.why: Rests on pain being the condition the plan's prescribed measures are directed at.

written.label: Passive drain
written.definition: A drain that removes fluid by gravity, capillary action or pressure differences arising in the body, without suction from an external source.
written.why: Rests on the absence of applied suction, which distinguishes passive from active drains.

written.label: Patient education plan specification
written.definition: A wound treatment plan specification that prescribes instructing the patient, and where applicable the patient's caregivers, about the wound, its care and the behaviours the patient is to carry out or avoid during treatment.
written.why: The differentia is that the plan prescribes conveying information and instruction to the patient rather than acting on the wound directly.

written.label: Penrose drain
written.definition: A capillary drain consisting of a soft, collapsible, thin-walled open tube that is placed in a wound and conducts fluid out along its inner and outer surfaces without applied suction.
written.why: The differentia rests on the standard construction of the Penrose drain as a soft, flat, collapsible tube that drains by capillarity and gravity.

written.label: Perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis plan specification
written.definition: A prophylaxis plan specification that prescribes the administration of one or more antimicrobial agents to a patient in the period immediately before, during or after a surgical procedure, with the objective of preventing surgical site infection.
written.why: The differentia rests on the established meaning: antimicrobial agents timed to the surgical procedure with the aim of preventing surgical site infection.

written.label: Peripheral arterial occlusive disease
written.definition: An angiopathy consisting in the narrowing or occlusion of the lumen of one or more arteries supplying the extremities, such that perfusion of the tissue of the affected limb is reduced.
written.why: The differentia is restriction to arteries of the limbs and to stenosis or occlusion of the lumen, which is the established meaning of peripheral arterial occlusive disease.

written.label: Phlegmon
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting in a purulent inflammation of soft connective tissue that spreads diffusely through the tissue and is not confined by a capsule.
written.why: The differentia rests on the established meaning of phlegmon as diffuse, non-encapsulated purulent soft-tissue inflammation, which distinguishes it from an abscess.

written.label: Pigtail catheter
written.definition: A passive drain consisting of a thin flexible catheter whose distal end curls into a loop once placed, holding the catheter in position, and that has side holes in the looped segment through which fluid enters.
written.why: The differentia rests on the defining feature of the pigtail catheter, its self-retaining coiled tip with side holes.

written.label: Plaster
written.definition: A fixing bandage consisting of a flexible backing strip coated on one side with a pressure-sensitive adhesive, that holds a dressing or device in place by adhering to the skin.
written.why: Under 'Fixing bandage' the label is taken in its sense of adhesive fixation tape, whose differentia is fixation by skin adhesion rather than by wrapping.

written.label: Polihexanide
written.definition: A biguanide that is a polymer whose repeating unit consists of a biguanide group linked to a hexamethylene chain.
written.why: The differentia rests on the chemical structure of polihexanide (polyhexamethylene biguanide).

written.label: Polihexanide containing solution
written.definition: An antiseptic solution that has polihexanide as an active antiseptic ingredient.
written.why: The differentia is the presence of polihexanide as the antiseptic agent, as stated in the label.

written.label: Polihexanide gel
written.definition: A wound gel/ointment/cream that has a semi-solid, water-based gel consistency and contains polihexanide as an active antiseptic ingredient.
written.why: The differentia rests on the gel form, which sets it apart from ointments and creams, and on polihexanide as its active ingredient.

written.label: Polyfilament thread material
written.definition: A material entity consisting of surgical suture thread in which each strand is made of multiple filaments braided or twisted together.
written.why: The differentia rests on the established meaning of polyfilament (multifilament) suture material as composed of several filaments, unlike monofilament thread.

written.label: Postoperative wound control process
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process in which a surgical wound is inspected and assessed after the operation that created it, to monitor its healing and to detect wound complications.
written.why: The differentia is that the assessed wound is a surgical wound and the assessment takes place after the operation to monitor healing.

written.label: Wound healing by primary intention process
written.definition: A wound healing in which the directly approximated edges of a wound with little tissue loss join together, so that the wound closes with minimal granulation tissue formation and leaves a narrow scar.
written.why: The differentia rests on the established surgical meaning of primary intention healing: closure by apposition of wound edges without substantial granulation.

written.label: Purulent exudate
written.definition: A wound exudate that is opaque and viscous and consists predominantly of neutrophils, cellular debris and liquefied necrotic tissue.
written.why: The differentia rests on the composition and appearance of pus, which distinguish it from serous or haemorrhagic exudate.

written.label: Redon drain
written.definition: A high-vacuum drain consisting of a perforated plastic tube placed in a wound and connected to a closed collecting bottle that is evacuated before use, so that the negative pressure in the bottle draws fluid out of the wound.
written.why: The differentia rests on the standard design of the Redon drain as a closed system with a pre-evacuated collecting bottle.

written.label: Regenerative wound healing process
written.definition: A wound healing in which the tissue lost in the wound is replaced by newly formed tissue of the same type, restoring the original tissue architecture and function without scar formation.
written.why: The differentia rests on the established meaning of regeneration as like-for-like tissue replacement without scarring.

written.label: Tissue repair process
written.definition: A wound healing related physiological process in which damaged or lost tissue is replaced by newly formed tissue, by regeneration, by scar formation or both, so that the continuity of the injured tissue is restored.
written.why: The definition follows the pathology usage of repair as the umbrella for regeneration and scar formation, which implies that 'Scarring process' should be its subclass rather than its sibling.

written.label: Resorbable thread material
written.definition: A material entity consisting of surgical suture thread made of a material that, after implantation, is degraded by hydrolysis or enzymatic action in the body and absorbed, so that it does not have to be removed.
written.why: The differentia rests on the established meaning of resorbable (absorbable) suture material as degraded and absorbed by the body.

written.label: Ringer solution
written.definition: A wound irrigation solution consisting of sodium chloride, potassium chloride and calcium chloride dissolved in water, isotonic with blood plasma.
written.why: Rests on the established composition of Ringer's solution as a balanced electrolyte solution.

written.label: Robinson drain
written.definition: A gravity drain that is a closed passive system consisting of a soft perforated tube leading from the wound or body cavity into a sealed collection bag.
written.why: Rests on the Robinson drain being a closed, non-suction tube-and-bag drain.

written.label: Sanguine exudate
written.definition: A wound exudate that consists predominantly of fresh blood and is thin and red.
written.why: Rests on the standard wound-care description of sanguineous drainage as bloody exudate.

written.label: Pathological scarring process
written.definition: A disorder development process in which the fibrous tissue laid down during wound repair is deposited in excess or in a disorganized way, so that the repair results in an abnormal scar.
written.why: Rests on pathological scarring being deviant fibrotic repair, in contrast to the sibling process of wound edge separation.

written.label: Scratch wound
written.definition: A traumatic wound that is the output of a sharp or rough object being drawn across the skin surface, producing a superficial linear disruption of the skin.
written.why: Rests on the mechanism and linear, superficial shape that distinguish a scratch from other traumatic wounds.

written.label: Secondary dressing
written.definition: A wound dressing that is placed over a primary dressing and does not itself contact the wound bed.
written.why: Rests on the wound-care distinction between primary and secondary dressings by position relative to the wound bed.

written.label: Wound healing by secondary intention process
written.definition: A wound healing in which the wound edges are not approximated and the tissue defect is closed by the formation of granulation tissue, wound contraction and epithelialization.
written.why: Rests on the surgical definition of secondary intention as healing of an open wound from its base.

written.label: Semi-open drain
written.definition: A drain consisting of a tube that leads fluid out of the wound into a dressing or an unsealed receptacle, so that the drainage pathway remains open to the environment.
written.why: Rests on the semi-open drain being a tube drain that, unlike a closed drain, does not end in a sealed collection system.

written.label: Seroma
written.definition: A material disease entity that is a collection of serous fluid accumulated in a tissue space or surgically created dead space, consisting of neither pus nor blood.
written.why: Rests on the clinical definition of a seroma as a localized serous fluid collection, distinct from abscess and hematoma.

written.label: Serosanguineous exudate
written.definition: A wound exudate that is thin, watery and pale red to pink, consisting of serous fluid mixed with a small amount of blood.
written.why: Rests on the standard wound-care description of serosanguineous drainage as a mixture of serum and blood.

written.label: Serous exudate
written.definition: A wound exudate that is thin, watery and clear to pale yellow, consisting of plasma-derived fluid without appreciable blood or pus.
written.why: Rests on the standard wound-care description of serous drainage as clear plasma fluid.

written.label: Shea classification of pressure ulcers
written.definition: A wound classification scale that grades pressure ulcers according to Shea by the deepest tissue layer involved, from the epidermis and dermis through subcutaneous fat and deep fascia to bone.
written.why: Rests on Shea's grading of pressure ulcers by depth of tissue involvement, parallel to the depth-based sibling burn scale.

written.label: Silicone spacer grid
written.definition: A wound dressing consisting of a thin perforated silicone sheet that is placed in direct contact with the wound bed and through whose openings exudate passes to an overlying dressing.
written.why: Rests on the silicone spacer grid being a perforated silicone wound contact layer.

written.label: Silver-containing wound dressing
written.definition: A wound dressing that has silver, in elemental, ionic or compound form, incorporated as a component bearing an antimicrobial agent role.
written.why: Rests on the presence of silver as the incorporated antimicrobial component that sets these dressings apart.

written.label: Simple interrupted suture
written.definition: A suture in situ consisting of a single stitch that passes through both wound edges and is knotted and cut separately from any adjacent stitch.
written.why: Rests on the surgical definition of the interrupted stitch as individually tied, independent of neighbouring stitches.

written.label: Skin color assessment process
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process in which the hue of the skin in and around the wound is inspected and that has as specified output a datum about that hue.
written.why: Rests on skin color assessment being an inspection of wound and periwound skin hue, styled after the sibling measurement process.

written.label: Skin graft
written.definition: A material entity that is a portion of skin, comprising epidermis and part or all of the dermis, that has been separated from its donor site and its blood supply and is transferred to a recipient site.
written.why: Rests on the surgical definition of a skin graft as skin transferred without its own vascular supply.

written.label: Skin grafting plan specification
written.definition: A wound treatment plan specification that prescribes harvesting a skin graft from a donor site and fixing it onto the wound bed as the recipient site.
written.why: Rests on skin grafting being the planned transfer of donor skin onto a wound.

written.label: Skin stapling plan specification
written.definition: A wound closure technique plan specification that prescribes approximating the skin edges of a wound with metal staples inserted by a stapling device.
written.why: Rests on skin stapling being closure of the skin by staples rather than by sutures or adhesives.

written.label: Smoking
written.definition: A process in which a person inhales and exhales the smoke produced by burning tobacco or another plant material.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of smoking as the inhalation of combustion smoke, matching the sibling process definitions.

written.label: Wound odor assessment process
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process that examines the presence, intensity and character of the odor emanating from a wound and has as specified output a datum about that wound odor.
written.why: The differentia rests on the wound feature assessed (odor) and its output datum, following the sibling's output-based style.

written.label: Split-thickness skin graft
written.definition: A skin graft that consists of the epidermis together with only part of the thickness of the underlying dermis of the donor site.
written.why: The differentia rests on the standard surgical meaning of split-thickness, which is partial-dermis harvest as opposed to full-thickness grafts.

written.label: Substance used for enzymatic wound debridement
written.definition: A material used for wound treatment that contains exogenous enzymes which, when applied to a wound, degrade necrotic tissue and devitalized extracellular matrix so that they can be removed from the wound bed.
written.why: The differentia rests on the enzymatic mechanism that defines enzymatic debridement, distinguishing it from sibling materials such as antiseptic agents.

written.label: Surgical treatment process
written.definition: A disease disorder treatment process in which the disease or disorder is treated by an operative manual and instrumental intervention on the patient's body, such as incision, excision, manipulation or repair of tissue.
written.why: The differentia rests on the operative, instrumental mode of intervention that distinguishes surgical treatment from other treatments.

written.label: Surgical wound debridement process
written.definition: A debridement process in which necrotic, devitalized or infected tissue and foreign material are removed from a wound by sharp excision with surgical instruments.
written.why: The differentia rests on the sharp, instrument-based removal technique that distinguishes surgical debridement from enzymatic, autolytic or mechanical debridement.

written.label: Suture in situ
written.definition: A device consisting of suture material that has been placed through or around tissue of a patient and secured there so that it holds the tissue in apposition or in position.
written.why: The differentia rests on the suture being located in the patient's tissue and on its tissue-holding function, as 'in situ' indicates.

written.label: Suturing plan specification
written.definition: A wound closure technique plan specification that prescribes approximating the wound edges by passing a needle with attached suture material through the tissue on both sides of the wound and securing the thread.
written.why: The differentia rests on the needle-and-thread approximation technique that distinguishes suturing from other closure techniques such as stapling or adhesive strips.

written.label: Synthetic wound dressing foam
written.definition: A wound dressing that consists of a porous, absorbent foam made of a synthetic polymer.
written.why: The differentia rests on the dressing's material form (foam) and its synthetic polymer composition.

written.label: Systemic antibiotic therapy plan specification
written.definition: An antibiotic therapy plan specification that prescribes administering an antibiotic by an enteral or parenteral route so that it is distributed throughout the body via the bloodstream.
written.why: The differentia rests on the systemic route and distribution, as opposed to topical or local antibiotic therapy.

written.label: Taking a wound swab
written.definition: A diagnostic process to assess wound characteristics in which a swab is passed over the wound bed to collect a specimen of wound material for laboratory examination.
written.why: The differentia rests on the swab-based specimen collection from the wound that defines taking a wound swab.

written.label: Wound healing by tertiary intention process
written.definition: A wound healing in which the wound is initially left open and only closed surgically after a delay, with healing proceeding after this delayed primary closure.
written.why: The differentia rests on the standard meaning of tertiary intention, which is delayed primary closure as opposed to immediate closure or spontaneous healing of an open wound.

written.label: Thermal wound
written.definition: A traumatic wound that is the output of a wound causing heat impact process, in which tissue is damaged by the action of excessive heat.
written.why: The differentia rests on the given axiom that the wound is output of a wound causing heat impact process.

written.label: Thoracic drain
written.definition: A drain that is inserted through the chest wall into the pleural cavity or mediastinum to evacuate air, fluid or blood from it.
written.why: The differentia rests on the thoracic location of insertion and drainage that distinguishes a chest drain from other drains.

written.label: Thread size
written.definition: A size that inheres in a surgical suture thread and corresponds to a designation of its diameter in a standardized suture sizing scale.
written.why: The differentia rests on the bearer being a suture thread and on the size being expressed by a standardized suture size designation.

written.label: Thread size 0
written.definition: A thread size that corresponds to the suture size designation 0 of the United States Pharmacopeia scale, next larger than 2-0 and next smaller than 1.
written.why: The differentia rests on the named USP size designation and its position in the size scale.

written.label: Thread size 1
written.definition: A thread size that corresponds to the suture size designation 1 of the United States Pharmacopeia scale, next larger than 0 and next smaller than 2.
written.why: The differentia rests on the named USP size designation and its position in the size scale.

written.label: Thread size 10-0
written.definition: A thread size that corresponds to the suture size designation 10-0 of the United States Pharmacopeia scale, next smaller than 9-0 and next larger than 11-0.
written.why: The differentia rests on the named USP size designation and its position in the size scale.

written.label: Thread size 11-0
written.definition: A thread size that corresponds to the suture size designation 11-0 of the United States Pharmacopeia scale, next smaller than 10-0.
written.why: The differentia rests on the named USP size designation and its position in the size scale.

written.label: Thread size 12-0
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 12-0, one step finer than 11-0 on the suture size scale, on which sizes written n-0 become finer as n increases.
written.why: Rests on the position of the designation 12-0 on the ordinal suture size scale; no diameter is stated because diameter ranges differ between suture material classes.

written.label: Thread size 13-0
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 13-0, one step finer than 12-0 on the suture size scale, on which sizes written n-0 become finer as n increases.
written.why: Rests on the position of 13-0 on the ordinal n-0 size scale; it is not asserted to be a USP pharmacopoeial size, which may not list it.

written.label: Thread size 2
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 2, one step coarser than 1 on the suture size scale, on which sizes written as whole numbers become coarser as the number increases.
written.why: Rests on the position of the designation 2 on the ordinal suture size scale above size 1.

written.label: Thread size 2-0
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 2-0, one step finer than 0 and one step coarser than 3-0 on the suture size scale.
written.why: Rests on the position of 2-0 between 0 and 3-0 on the ordinal suture size scale.

written.label: Thread size 3
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 3, one step coarser than 2 on the suture size scale, on which sizes written as whole numbers become coarser as the number increases.
written.why: Rests on the position of the designation 3 on the ordinal suture size scale above size 2.

written.label: Thread size 3-0
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 3-0, one step finer than 2-0 and one step coarser than 4-0 on the suture size scale.
written.why: Rests on the position of 3-0 between 2-0 and 4-0 on the ordinal suture size scale.

written.label: Thread size 4
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 4, one step coarser than 3 on the suture size scale, on which sizes written as whole numbers become coarser as the number increases.
written.why: Rests on the position of the designation 4 on the ordinal suture size scale above size 3.

written.label: Thread size 4-0
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 4-0, one step finer than 3-0 and one step coarser than 5-0 on the suture size scale.
written.why: Rests on the position of 4-0 between 3-0 and 5-0 on the ordinal suture size scale.

written.label: Thread size 5
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 5, one step coarser than 4 on the suture size scale, on which sizes written as whole numbers become coarser as the number increases.
written.why: Rests on the position of the designation 5 on the ordinal suture size scale above size 4.

written.label: Thread size 5-0
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 5-0, one step finer than 4-0 and one step coarser than 6-0 on the suture size scale.
written.why: Rests on the position of 5-0 between 4-0 and 6-0 on the ordinal suture size scale.

written.label: Thread size 6-0
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 6-0, one step finer than 5-0 and one step coarser than 7-0 on the suture size scale.
written.why: Rests on the position of 6-0 between 5-0 and 7-0 on the ordinal suture size scale.

written.label: Thread size 7-0
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 7-0, one step finer than 6-0 and one step coarser than 8-0 on the suture size scale.
written.why: Rests on the position of 7-0 between 6-0 and 8-0 on the ordinal suture size scale.

written.label: Thread size 8-0
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 8-0, one step finer than 7-0 and one step coarser than 9-0 on the suture size scale.
written.why: Rests on the position of 8-0 between 7-0 and 9-0 on the ordinal suture size scale.

written.label: Thread size 9-0
written.definition: A thread size that is the suture size designation 9-0, one step finer than 8-0 and one step coarser than 10-0 on the suture size scale.
written.why: Rests on the position of 9-0 between 8-0 and 10-0 on the ordinal suture size scale.

written.label: Topical antibiotic therapy plan specification
written.definition: An antibiotic therapy plan specification that prescribes applying an antibiotic agent directly onto the surface of the skin, a mucous membrane or a wound at the site to be treated rather than giving it systemically.
written.why: Rests on the topical route of administration, which distinguishes it from systemic antibiotic therapy plans.

written.label: Transparent polyurethane film
written.definition: A wound dressing that consists of a thin, transparent, semipermeable sheet of polyurethane through which the covered wound can be inspected.
written.why: Rests on the material, thin film form, transparency and semipermeability that define film dressings in wound care.

written.label: Trauma process
written.definition: A process in which a sudden external mechanical force acts on a tissue.
written.why: Rests on mechanical injury by an abrupt external force, distinguishing it from the sustained pressure, chemical and perfusion sibling processes.

written.label: Tscherne and Oestern wound classification
written.definition: A wound classification scale that grades the severity of the soft-tissue injury accompanying a closed or open fracture.
written.why: Rests on the established Tscherne and Oestern scheme for grading soft-tissue damage in closed and open fractures.

written.label: Tscherne and Oestern wound classification grade
written.definition: A wound classification grade that is a category of the Tscherne and Oestern wound classification.
written.why: Follows the sibling pattern: the grade is a category of the named classification scale.

written.label: Tympanic drain
written.definition: A drain that is a small tube placed through an incision in the tympanic membrane so that the middle ear is ventilated and fluid can drain from it.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of the tympanostomy (ventilation) tube and its placement through the eardrum.

written.label: Ulcus cruris mixtum
written.definition: A skin wound that is an ulcer of the lower leg in a patient who has both chronic venous insufficiency and peripheral arterial disease, so that venous and arterial disorders together form its pathogenic background.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of ulcus cruris mixtum as a leg ulcer of combined venous and arterial origin.

written.label: Ulcus cruris venosum
written.definition: A venous insufficiency wound that is an ulcer of the skin of the lower leg.
written.why: The first parent supplies the venous insufficiency context; the differentia adds the skin from the second parent and the lower-leg site of an ulcus cruris.

written.label: Ulcus hypertonicus Martorell
written.definition: A skin wound that is an ulcer of the lower leg resulting from ischemic necrosis of the skin caused by stenosing arteriolosclerosis of subcutaneous arterioles in a patient with arterial hypertension.
written.why: Rests on the established description of Martorell's hypertensive ischemic leg ulcer.

written.label: Ultrasound-assisted wound debridement process
written.definition: A debridement process in which devitalized tissue, debris and biofilm are detached from a wound bed by ultrasonic energy transmitted through a fluid applied to the wound.
written.why: Differentia is the energy source and mechanism that distinguish this method from other debridement methods.

written.label: Ventricular drain
written.definition: A drain that is inserted through the skull into a cerebral ventricle to conduct cerebrospinal fluid out of the ventricular system.
written.why: Rests on the standard meaning of a ventricular drain in neurosurgery: its site and the fluid it removes.

written.label: Vertical mattress suture
written.definition: A suture in situ in which each stitch crosses the wound twice in a plane perpendicular to the wound edge, with one deep pass placed far from the wound edge and one superficial pass placed near it, and is tied on the side where it entered.
written.why: Rests on the defining stitch geometry of the vertical mattress suture as opposed to simple and horizontal mattress sutures.

written.label: Wagner and Anderson wound classification grade
written.definition: A wound classification grade that is a category of the Wagner and Anderson wound classification.
written.why: Follows the sibling pattern: a grade is defined by the scale it belongs to, which holds whatever that scale's content turns out to be.

written.label: Water-jet assisted wound debridement process
written.definition: A debridement process in which devitalized tissue and debris are cut away from a wound and removed by a high-velocity jet of sterile liquid.
written.why: Differentia is the hydrosurgical mechanism, a pressurized liquid jet, that distinguishes it from sharp, ultrasonic and other debridement.

written.label: Wearing sterile gloves plan specification
written.definition: An aseptic cuticle plan specification that prescribes that persons coming into contact with a wound or sterile field cover their hands with gloves that are free of viable microorganisms.
written.why: The parent label most likely renders the German 'aseptische Kautelen' (aseptic precautions); this precaution is specifically about covering the hands with sterile gloves.

written.label: Wound dehiscence causally related to suture insufficiency
written.definition: A wound dehiscence that is the output of a wound dehiscence process caused by the failure of the sutures holding the wound edges together to keep them approximated.
written.why: Differentia is the cause named in the label, failure of the suture material or suture technique, placed within the parent's process-based pattern.

written.label: Wound and soft tissue drain
written.definition: A drain that is placed in a wound or in soft tissue to conduct accumulated fluid out of it.
written.why: Distinguishes the drain by its site of placement, wound or soft tissue, as opposed to body-cavity or ventricular drains.

written.label: Wound base
written.definition: A material entity that is part of a wound and consists of the tissue forming the floor of the wound, bounded by the wound edges.
written.why: Rests on the part_of some Wound axiom and the clinical meaning of wound base as the wound floor whose granulation, necrosis, fibrin and epithelialization are assessed.

written.label: Wound biofilm
written.definition: A material entity that is a structured community of microorganisms embedded in a self-produced extracellular polymeric matrix and attached to the surface or tissue of a wound.
written.why: Rests on the established microbiological definition of biofilm, located in a wound.

written.label: Wound cleansing process
written.definition: A wound treatment process in which non-adherent material, exudate and microorganisms are removed from the wound surface and surrounding skin by rinsing or wiping with a cleansing solution, without excising tissue.
written.why: Differentia is the removal of loose material by fluid application, which distinguishes cleansing from debridement and other treatments.

written.label: Wound closure process
written.definition: A wound treatment process that brings the edges of a wound into apposition or covers the wound defect with tissue, so that the wound is no longer open.
written.why: Rests on the surgical meaning of wound closure, which covers both primary approximation and coverage by graft or flap.

written.label: Wound closure technique plan specification
written.definition: A treatment plan specification that prescribes the method and means by which a wound is to be closed in a wound closure process.
written.why: Differentia is that the plan concerns how a wound closure is to be carried out.

written.label: Wound contraction process
written.definition: A wound healing related physiological process in which myofibroblasts in the granulation tissue draw the wound edges centripetally toward each other, reducing the area of the open wound.
written.why: Rests on the established cellular mechanism of wound contraction, which distinguishes it from scarring and epithelialization.

written.label: Wound diagnostic process
written.definition: A disease diagnostic process that is directed at a wound of a patient and assesses whether it is present and what its nature and characteristics are.
written.why: The differentia rests on the wound being the object assessed, which separates it from diagnostic processes directed at other disease entities.

written.label: Wound documentation process
written.definition: A planned process in which observations and findings about a wound of a patient are recorded in an information artifact.
written.why: The differentia rests on the recording of wound-related information as the output of the planned process.

written.label: Wound dressing composed of a polylactide membrane
written.definition: A wound-integrating wound dressing that consists of a membrane made of polylactide, a resorbable polymer of lactic acid.
written.why: The differentia rests on the dressing's material, a polylactide membrane, which separates it from other wound-integrating dressings.

written.label: Wound dressing composed of polyurethane foam
written.definition: A wound-integrating wound dressing that consists of a porous foam matrix made of polyurethane.
written.why: The differentia rests on the dressing's material, a polyurethane foam; wound-integration is inherited from the parent.

written.label: Wound edge
written.definition: A material entity that is part of a wound and consists of the tissue at the margin of the wound where the wound bed adjoins the surrounding intact skin.
written.why: The definition rests on the asserted part-of-wound axiom and the standard clinical meaning of the wound margin, and it is consistent with the maceration and skin-adherence qualities.

written.label: Wound edge protection process
written.definition: A wound treatment process in which the wound edge is shielded from agents and forces that would damage it, such as exudate or adhesive stripping.
written.why: The differentia rests on the wound edge, rather than the wound bed, being the protected target of the treatment.

written.label: Wound expert role
written.definition: A health care provider role that is borne by a person holding a specialised qualification in wound care and that is realized in the assessment and treatment of patients' wounds.
written.why: The differentia rests on the specialised wound-care qualification and on the role being realized in wound assessment and treatment.

written.label: Wound exudate
written.definition: A material entity that is fluid released from the tissues of a wound, derived from blood plasma that has passed from the vasculature into the wound.
written.why: The differentia rests on the established meaning of exudate as plasma-derived fluid that emerges from a wound.

written.label: Wound gel/ointment/cream
written.definition: A clinical drug product that has a semisolid dosage form and is intended for topical application to a wound.
written.why: The differentia rests on the semisolid dosage form shared by gels, ointments and creams and on topical application to wounds.

written.label: Wound healing disorder
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting in the abnormal organization of the tissues of and around a wound of a patient, such that the wound does not progress through healing in the expected manner.
written.why: The differentia follows the comments, which treat the disorder as an abnormal material organisation in and around the wound that impairs healing, and it matches the style of the 'Diabetic metabolic disorder' sibling.

written.label: Wound healing related physiological process
written.definition: A biological_process that occurs in an organism after tissue injury and is part of the restoration of the integrity of the injured tissue.
written.why: The differentia rests on the processes being physiological contributions to the repair of injured tissue.

written.label: Wound infection process
written.definition: A course of the disease process in which pathogenic microorganisms invade and multiply in the tissue of a wound and elicit a host response.
written.why: The differentia rests on microbial invasion and multiplication within wound tissue, which separates it from the malignant, autoimmune and venous sibling processes.

written.label: Wound irrigation process
written.definition: A wound treatment process in which a flow of liquid is applied to a wound to rinse debris, exudate and microorganisms from its surface.
written.why: The differentia rests on the mechanical rinsing of the wound with a liquid flow.

written.label: Wound irrigation solution
written.definition: A clinical drug product that is a liquid formulated for rinsing a wound in a wound irrigation process.
written.why: The differentia rests on the product's liquid form and on its use in wound irrigation.

written.label: Wound manager role
written.definition: A health care provider role that is borne by a person holding a qualification in wound management and that is realized in organising and coordinating the wound care of patients.
written.why: The differentia rests on the coordinating and organising function of the wound manager, which separates it from the wound expert role.

written.label: Wound development process
written.definition: A disorder development process in which a wound comes into being in a patient through disruption of the continuity of body tissue.
written.why: The differentia rests on the coming into being of the wound itself, which separates it from the dehiscence process and from the wound causing process that brings it about.

written.label: Wound palpation
written.definition: A diagnostic process to assess wound characteristics in which an examiner touches and presses the wound and the surrounding tissue with the hands to perceive their physical properties.
written.why: The differentia rests on manual tactile examination as the method of assessment.

written.label: Wound spacer grid
written.definition: A wound dressing that is a non-adherent open-mesh layer placed in direct contact with the wound bed, which separates the wound from a secondary dressing and lets exudate pass through it.
written.why: The differentia rests on the established meaning of a spacer grid (German 'Wunddistanzgitter') as a non-adherent mesh wound contact layer.

written.label: Wound temperature assessment process
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process that has as specified output a datum about the temperature of the wound bed or of the periwound skin.
written.why: The differentia rests on the specified output (a temperature datum) and follows the style of the sibling size measurement process.

written.label: Wound treatment process
written.definition: A disease disorder treatment process that has as participant a wound and is directed at that wound's healing or management.
written.why: The differentia rests on the axiom 'has participant some Wound' and on the target of the treatment.

written.label: Wound volumetrics
written.definition: A wound size measurement process that has as specified output a datum about the volume of the wound cavity.
written.why: Volumetrics means measuring volume, which sets it apart from depth or area measurement; note that the parent's definition wrongly restricts its output to depth.

written.label: Wound with accompanying fracture
written.definition: A traumatic wound that is the output of a wound causing trauma process which also has as output a fracture of a bone in the same body region.
written.why: The differentia rests on the co-occurring fracture produced by the same trauma, as the label states.

written.label: Wounds classified according to Gustilo and Anderson
written.definition: A wound with accompanying fracture that is a skin wound through which the fracture site communicates with the outside of the body, i.e. the soft tissue wound of an open fracture graded by the Gustilo and Anderson classification.
written.why: The Gustilo and Anderson system grades only open fractures, so its wounds are breaches of the skin that communicate with the fracture.

written.label: T drain
written.definition: An abdominal drain consisting of a T-shaped tube whose short crossbar limbs lie in the lumen of the common bile duct and whose long limb leads out through the abdominal wall, bearing a function of draining bile externally.
written.why: The differentia rests on the established T-tube design and its placement in the bile duct for biliary drainage.
