written.label: Impaired wound healing process
written.definition: A wound healing that deviates from the normal orderly and timely sequence of healing phases, such that restoration of tissue integrity is delayed, arrested or yields abnormal tissue.
written.why: The differentia rests on deviation from normal healing, as the synonym 'pathological wound healing process' indicates.

written.label: Group A Streptococcus
written.definition: A pathogen that is a Gram-positive coccus of the genus Streptococcus bearing the Lancefield group A carbohydrate antigen in its cell wall.
written.why: The differentia rests on the Lancefield serogrouping that defines Group A Streptococcus.

written.label: Vancomycin
written.definition: A molecule of the glycopeptide vancomycin, a glycosylated tricyclic heptapeptide that binds the D-alanyl-D-alanine termini of peptidoglycan precursors and thereby inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis, and that has an antibiotic drug role.
written.why: The differentia rests on the chemical identity and mechanism of vancomycin, together with the asserted antibiotic drug role axiom.

written.label: Surgical site infection
written.definition: A material disease entity that is an infection by microorganisms of the surgical incision, of the tissues at the operative site or of an organ or space manipulated during a surgical operation, arising after that operation.
written.why: The differentia rests on the anatomical and temporal link of the infection to a preceding surgical operation.

written.label: Soft tissue wound
written.definition: A wound whose damaged tissue is non-osseous covering, connecting or supporting tissue of the body, such as skin, subcutis, fascia, muscle, tendon or ligament, rather than bone or a parenchymal organ.
written.why: The differentia rests on the kind of tissue affected, which is soft tissue as opposed to bone or organ parenchyma.

written.label: Laceration
written.definition: A traumatic wound in which tissue has been torn or split by blunt force, producing irregular wound margins.
written.why: The differentia rests on the tearing mechanism and the irregular margins that distinguish a laceration from incised or puncture wounds.

written.label: Acute wound
written.definition: A wound that has recently arisen and participates in a wound healing proceeding through the normal phases of repair in an orderly and timely sequence.
written.why: The differentia rests on the established wound care distinction between acute wounds, which heal in an orderly and timely way, and chronic wounds.

written.label: Foreign body
written.definition: A material entity that is located in a body part or wound of an organism, is not part of that organism, and has entered or been placed there from outside.
written.why: The differentia rests on the material's external origin and its location within the organism.

written.label: Hypertrophic scar
written.definition: A material entity that is a raised mass of excess collagenous scar tissue at the site of a healed wound, is the output of an excessive collagen deposition process, and remains confined to the boundaries of the original wound.
written.why: The differentia rests on the collagen deposition axiom and on confinement to the wound borders, which distinguishes it from a keloid.

written.label: Sepsis
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting in the abnormal organization of the organs or tissues of a patient, resulting from a dysregulated host response to an infection, such that organ function is impaired.
written.why: The differentia rests on the current consensus definition of sepsis as organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection, phrased in the style of the diabetic sibling.

written.label: Osteomyelitis
written.definition: A material disease entity that is a portion of bone, including its marrow, affected by inflammation.
written.why: The differentia rests on inflammation involving bone and marrow; the cause is left open because non-infectious forms of osteomyelitis exist.

written.label: Bacterial colonization process
written.definition: A process in which bacteria adhere to and multiply on the surface of or within a tissue of a host organism.
written.why: Rests on the established microbiological meaning of colonization as bacterial attachment and replication on a host tissue.

written.label: Pressure offloading process
written.definition: A wound treatment process that realizes a pressure redistribution function, in which mechanical load on the wound site is reduced or removed.
written.why: Rests on the realizes axiom and the clinical meaning of offloading as relieving load from a wound area.

written.label: Prophylactic antibiotic therapy plan specification
written.definition: A prophylaxis plan specification that prescribes giving a substance bearing an antibiotic drug role to a patient to prevent a bacterial infection.
written.why: Rests on the label: the prophylactic aim is prevention of infection and the means is an antibiotic.

written.label: Pressure redistribution mattress
written.definition: A device that is a support surface on which a recumbent person lies and that bears a pressure redistribution function.
written.why: Rests on the has function axiom and on a mattress being a lying surface, which distinguishes it from footwear and dressings.

written.label: Therapeutic footwear
written.definition: A device that is worn on the foot and bears a pressure redistribution function acting on the surfaces of the foot.
written.why: Rests on the has function axiom and on footwear being worn on the foot, which distinguishes it from the mattress.

written.label: Bacterial culture process
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process in which a specimen taken from a wound is incubated in a growth medium so that bacteria present in it multiply and can be detected and identified.
written.why: Rests on the standard laboratory meaning of a bacterial culture applied to a wound specimen.

written.label: Vascular assessment process
written.definition: A wound diagnostic process that evaluates the condition of the blood vessels supplying or draining the body region in which a wound is located.
written.why: Rests on the clinical meaning of vascular assessment as the evaluation of the blood supply relevant to a wound.

written.label: Ankle-brachial index measurement process
written.definition: A vascular assessment process that has as specified output the ratio of the systolic blood pressure measured at the ankle to the systolic blood pressure measured at the arm.
written.why: Rests on the standard definition of the ankle-brachial index as an ankle-to-arm systolic pressure ratio.

written.label: Wound photography process
written.definition: A wound documentation process in which a photographic image of a wound is produced as a record of its appearance.
written.why: Rests on the label: the documentation is done by capturing an image of the wound.

written.label: Wound healing criterion
written.definition: A threshold specification that specifies a value of a wound attribute whose attainment indicates that a wound has healed or has reached a specified stage of healing.
written.why: Rests on the parent being a threshold and the label tying it to the judgement of wound healing.

written.label: Epithelialization criterion
written.definition: A wound healing criterion that is about the degree of epithelialization of a wound, specifying the extent of epithelial coverage of the wound surface to be attained.
written.why: Rests on the is about axiom pointing to degree of epithelialization.

written.label: antibiotic drug role
written.definition: A clinical drug role borne by a substance used to kill bacteria or inhibit their growth.
written.why: Rests on the established pharmacological meaning of antibiotic, phrased in the style of the sibling definition.

written.label: Process of drug administration
written.definition: A process in which a material entity bearing a clinical drug role is introduced into or applied onto the body of a patient.
written.why: Rests on the has participant axiom and the clinical meaning of giving a drug to a patient.

written.label: pressure redistribution function
written.definition: A function that is realized by spreading the mechanical load exerted on a body surface over a larger contact area or over time, thereby lowering the pressure on any single region.
written.why: Rests on the wound care meaning of pressure redistribution as load spreading by area or by time.

written.label: Surgical debridement plan specification
written.definition: A treatment plan specification that prescribes the removal of necrotic, infected or devitalized tissue from a wound by means of surgical instruments.
written.why: Rests on the surgical meaning of debridement as the instrumental excision of non-viable tissue.

written.label: therapeutic role
written.definition: A role that is borne by an entity in virtue of its being used to treat, alleviate or cure a disease of a patient.
written.why: Rests on the medical meaning of therapeutic as serving the treatment of disease.

written.label: clinical function
written.definition: A function whose realization serves the prevention, diagnosis, treatment or monitoring of a disease in a patient.
written.why: Rests on clinical meaning a function directed at the care of patients with respect to disease.

written.label: therapeutic function
written.definition: A clinical function whose realization contributes to the treatment of a disease of a patient.
written.why: Rests on therapeutic narrowing clinical purposes to treatment, as opposed to diagnosis, prevention or monitoring.

written.label: Inflammation process
written.definition: A wound healing related physiological process in which, in response to tissue injury, local blood vessels dilate and become more permeable and leukocytes migrate into the wound to clear debris and microorganisms.
written.why: Rests on the established description of the inflammatory phase of wound healing, in the style of the scarring sibling.

written.label: wound protection function
written.definition: A function that is realized by shielding a wound from mechanical injury, contamination or other harmful external influences.
written.why: Rests on the label: the function protects the wound from external harm.

written.label: wound dressing layer function
written.definition: A function that is borne by a layer of a wound dressing and is realized in processes in which that layer contributes to the action of the dressing on the wound.
written.why: Rests on reading the label as the function of a component layer of a wound dressing.

written.label: wound dressing fixation function
written.definition: A function that is realized in holding a wound dressing in place on or over a wound.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of fixing a dressing in position.

written.label: non adhesive wound dressing fixation function
written.definition: A wound dressing fixation function that is realized without its bearer adhering to the patient's skin.
written.why: Sets it apart from adhesive fixation by the absence of adhesion to the skin.

written.label: wound moisture absorbance function
written.definition: A function that is realized in the uptake of exudate or other fluid from a wound into the bearer.
written.why: Rests on absorption, meaning fluid taken up from the wound into the material.

written.label: wound moisture regulation function
written.definition: A function that is realized in keeping the moisture of a wound bed from becoming either excessive or insufficient, by taking up fluid from the wound or by retaining or supplying fluid to it.
written.why: Rests on regulation, which, unlike mere absorption, maintains wound-bed moisture in both directions.

written.label: wound desinfecting function
written.definition: A function that is realized in killing or inactivating microorganisms in or on a wound.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of disinfecting (antisepsis) applied to a wound.

written.label: wound edge approximating function
written.definition: A function that is realized in bringing the edges of a wound together and holding them in apposition.
written.why: Rests on the surgical meaning of approximating wound edges.

written.label: wound inspection facilitation function
written.definition: A function that is realized in making a wound more readily accessible to visual or other examination.
written.why: Rests on facilitating the examination of a wound; the definition is kept general to fit every bearer.

written.label: wound coverage function
written.definition: A function that is realized in covering a wound so that it is shielded from the external environment.
written.why: Rests on the established meaning of covering a wound.

written.label: Wound dressing process
written.definition: A wound treatment process in which a wound dressing is applied to or renewed on a wound.
written.why: Rests on the axioms naming a wound and a wound dressing as participants, plus the clinical meaning of dressing a wound.

written.label: wound classification grade
written.definition: A disease classification stage that is assigned to a wound under a wound grading system and ranks the wound according to its severity.
written.why: Rests on the meaning of a grade within a wound classification system.

written.label: Necrotic material
written.definition: A material disease entity consisting of a portion of a patient's tissue whose cells have died through pathological cell death while that portion remains within or attached to the body.
written.why: Rests on the medical meaning of necrotic tissue as dead tissue remaining in situ, matching the sibling style.

held.label: Aseptic cuticle plan specification
held.why: cannot: The label 'Aseptic cuticle' is unclear and appears to be a mistranslation of German 'aseptische Kautelen' (aseptic precautions), which would duplicate row 16, so the label needs correction first.

held.label: Bepanthen ointment
held.why: cannot: The class is named by a proprietary brand product, so a definition would have to use the brand name or would instead define a generic dexpanthenol ointment; the class should be relabelled or replaced by a generic class.

held.label: Bismuth III bromide
held.why: cannot: Inorganic bismuth(III) bromide is not an established wound antiseptic, and the label probably conflates it with bismuth tribromophenate, so the intended substance is unclear.

held.label: Hand disinfection plan specification
held.why: cannot: The parent label 'Aseptic cuticle plan specification' is unclear and probably a mistranslation of 'aseptische Kautelen' (aseptic precautions), so the required genus would be misleading until the parent is corrected.

held.label: Immunosuppression
held.why: cannot: Immunosuppression names a reduced capacity of the immune system or the act of suppressing it (a disposition, state or process, often intended therapy), not a material entity classified as pathological, so the parent does not fit.

held.label: Planimetry
held.why: cannot: Planimetry measures wound surface area, but the parent is defined as having a wound depth measurement datum as output, so any genus-differentia definition would assert something false; the parent definition must first be corrected to cover wound size in general.

held.label: Redness
held.why: cannot: 'Redness' cannot be distinguished from its sibling 'reddened', which already names the reddened colour of a bearer, so the classes appear to be duplicates and should be merged or clarified.

held.label: Surface disinfection plan specification
held.why: cannot: The parent label 'Aseptic cuticle plan specification' is unclear and apparently concerns skin, whereas surface disinfection usually refers to inanimate surfaces, so the parent does not demonstrably fit the label.

held.label: Thread size 1-0
held.why: cannot: In USP notation 1-0 is an alternative writing of size 0, so this class appears to duplicate 'Thread size 0' and no distinct differentia can be written.

held.label: URGE scale
held.why: cannot: No established wound classification scale named URGE is known, and nothing is given that says what it classifies or how.

held.label: Voltaren gel
held.why: cannot: The label is a brand name of a topical diclofenac preparation for application to intact skin, which does not fit the parent wound gel/ointment/cream, and brand names are excluded.

held.label: Wagner and Anderson wound classification
held.why: cannot: It is unclear which scale 'Wagner and Anderson' denotes (it is not a recognized name of the Meggitt-Wagner or another established wound scale), so its content cannot be stated without guessing.

held.label: Wound fabric adhesive plan specification
held.why: cannot: The label 'fabric adhesive' is ambiguous: it could mean a tissue adhesive (a likely mistranslation of German 'Gewebekleber') or fabric adhesive closure strips, so the technique specified cannot be determined without guessing.

held.label: Wound pocket
held.why: cannot: A wound pocket is a cavity, i.e. a space (a BFO site or immaterial entity) extending beneath intact tissue, so the parent 'material entity' does not fit what the label names.

held.label: Wound staple plastering plan specification
held.why: cannot: The label is unclear: 'staple plastering' may mean skin closure with staples or closure with adhesive strips (a literal rendering of German 'Klammerpflaster'), and these are different techniques.

held.label: Wound-integrating wound dressing
held.why: cannot: 'Wound-integrating' is not an established wound care term; it might mean resorbable dressings incorporated into new tissue or something else, so any definition would be a guess.

held.label: Wounds classified according to Tscherne and Oestern
held.why: cannot: The Tscherne and Oestern system also grades soft tissue injuries of closed fractures, where the skin may be intact, so the parent 'Skin wound' does not fit everything the label covers.

held.label: wound signaling function
held.why: cannot: The label is ambiguous: it could mean a dressing that indicates wound status or biological signalling in wound healing, and nothing in the row settles which.

held.label: first wound dressing layer function
held.why: cannot: The row does not say what makes a layer 'first', such as whether layers are counted from the wound side, so no sound differentia can be given.

held.label: second wound dressing layer function
held.why: cannot: The row does not say what makes a layer 'second' or how layers are ordered, so no sound differentia can be given.

held.label: wound infecting tendency
held.why: cannot: The label is ambiguous between a wound's tendency to become infected and an agent's tendency to infect wounds, and the row does not settle which.
